data.narrative:
Lightelligence is a public-stage semiconductor company that has raised $310M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of four same-sector, same-stage companies: Cerebras ($39.2B), Credo Semiconductor ($35.8B), Ouster ($2.3B), and Aeva Technologies ($1.1B). This universe spans a wide valuation range reflective of heterogeneous market valuations within frontier semiconductor hardware.

The peer-median method is the applicable triangulation approach here. The median valuation across these four public comparables is $19.0B, with a range floor of $1.1B and ceiling of $39.2B. Revenue-based multiples could not be applied because Lightelligence's revenue figures are not publicly available—a common constraint when valuing private semiconductor companies. The public semiconductor sector (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) trades at a 21.0x price-to-sales median, but this benchmark requires disclosed revenue to be actionable.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $16.2B to $21.9B, centered on the peer median of $19.0B. The primary uncertainty is Lightelligence's revenue profile and growth trajectory relative to peers, which would materially refine positioning within this range. The wide dispersion among peer valuations ($1.1B to $39.2B) also reflects sector-wide uncertainty around which frontier chip architectures will achieve sustainable market traction, arguing for caution around point estimates.
